chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

For the one praying, there are three characteristics: when he stands in his prayer, goodness descends upon him from the corners of the heaven to the crown of his head; and the angels surround him from his feet to the corners of the heaven; and an angel calls out, 'O you who pray! If you knew to Whom you are conversing privately, you would not miss it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and rewards of performing salat in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, the physical posture of prayer is depicted as a conduit for cosmic grace, where divine benevolence descends from the heavens and angels encircle the worshipper from head to toe. The presence of a specific angel who proclaims the majesty of the Divine emphasizes the concept of *muraqaba* (divine awareness), serving as a spiritual reminder to maintain reverence and prevent negligence (*ghaflah*) during the communion with Allah.
